question.problem: A painter has to paint all four sides of a fence. Which customary unit of measurement could the painter use to quantify the volume of paint he needs for each side?

current_example.problem:
A self-service restaurant offers ketchup in individual packets. Which customary unit of measurement could the restaurant use to quantify the volume of sauce in each packet?

I. ounces

II. fluid ounces

III. inches
current_example.worked_solution:
A table showing the customary units of volume is given below.

| Name | Symbol | Conversion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gallon | $\textrm{gal}$ | $1\,\textrm{gal} = 8\,\textrm{pints}$ |
| Pint | $\textrm{pt}$ | $1\,\textrm{pt} = 2\,\textrm{cups}$ |
| Cup | $-$ | $1\,\textrm{cup} = 8\,\textrm{fl oz}$ |
| Fluid ounce | $\textrm{fl oz}$ | $-$ |

Therefore, from the given options, the only unit of volume is "fluid ounce."
